1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.core: It saves massive amounts of resources because the pretraining phase is quite costly and generally requires data and computing resources that are out of the reach of most people and organizations.
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.case: To create the Llama 2 family of models, for example, Meta used A100-80 GB GPUs. Assuming renting such a GPU would cost $1.50/hr, the total costs of creating these models would exceed $5,000,000!
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.point: 预训练极其昂贵，微调让多数团队能在基础模型上低成本适配
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.explain: Llama 2 训练需大量 A100 GPU，成本超 500 万美元，说明预训练门槛极高；多数团队只能通过微调基础模型来适配任务。

1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.point: ChatGPT 的爆发标志着生成式 AI 走向大众
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.explain: ChatGPT 五天内达百万用户、两月内破亿，直观展示了大语言模型对交互方式的革命性影响。
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.core: 2022 marked the release of ChatGPT, which demonstrated how profoundly this technology was poised to revolutionize how we interact with technology and information.
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.case: 2022 marked the release of ChatGPT, which demonstrated how profoundly this technology was poised to revolutionize how we interact with technology and information. Reaching one million active users in five days and then one hundred million active users in two months, the new breed of AI models started out as human-like chatbots but quickly evolved into a monumental shift in our approach to common tasks, like translation, text generation, summarization, and more.

1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.point: 注意力机制让模型聚焦输入中相关的部分
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.explain: 在英荷翻译中，“lama’s”与“llamas”注意力高，与“I”注意力低，说明模型能根据相关性分配注意力。
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.core: Attention allows a model to focus on parts of the input sequence that are relevant to one another (“attend” to each other) and amplify their signal, as shown in Figure 1-14.
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.case: For instance, the output word “lama’s” is Dutch for “llamas,” which is why the attention between both is high. Similarly, the words “lama’s” and “I” have lower attention since they aren’t as related.

1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.point: 参数规模增长通常提升模型能力
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.explain: GPT-1 仅有 1.17 亿参数，作为早期模型代表，其规模远小于后续模型，印证参数增加与能力提升的关联。
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.core: If everything remains the same, we expect more parameters to greatly influence the capabilities and performance of language models.
1. An Introduction to Large Language Mod.case: GPT-1 was trained on a corpus of 7,000 books and Common Crawl, a large dataset of web pages. The resulting model consisted of 117 million parameters. Each parameter is a numerical value that represents the model’s understanding of language.

2. Tokens and Embeddings.core: This comparison will show us that newer tokenizers have changed their behavior to improve model performance, and we’ll also see how specialized models (like code generation models, for example) often need specialized tokenizers.
2. Tokens and Embeddings.case: The GPT-4 tokenizer represents the four spaces as a single token. In fact, it has a specific token for every sequence of whitespaces up to a list of 83 whitespaces. The Python keyword elif has its own token in GPT-4. Both this and the previous point stem from the model’s focus on code in addition to natural language.
2. Tokens and Embeddings.point: 分词器设计取决于训练目标，代码模型需要专门的分词器
2. Tokens and Embeddings.explain: GPT-4 分词器将四个空格视为单个 token，并为最多83个连续空格设置专用 token，且 Python 关键字 elif 有独立 token，这源于模型对代码的侧重，证明专用分词器能提升代码处理性能。

2. Tokens and Embeddings.point: 子词分词用##表示接续，未知词用[UNK]处理
2. Tokens and Embeddings.explain: BERT 分词结果中“capitalization”被拆为“capital”和“##ization”，##表示该 token 是前一个 token 的部分；未知词用[UNK]表示，具体展示了 WordPiece 子词分词及未知词处理方式。
2. Tokens and Embeddings.core: The ## characters are used to indicate this token is a partial token connected to the token that precedes it.
2. Tokens and Embeddings.case: [CLS] english and capital ##ization [UNK] [UNK] show _ token ##s false none eli ##f = = > = else : two tab ##s : " " three tab ##s : " " 12 . 0 * 50 = 600 [SEP]

2. Tokens and Embeddings.point: 面向代码的模型为每个数字分配独立 token
2. Tokens and Embeddings.explain: StarCoder2 分词器将“12.0*50=600”切分为“1 2 . 0 * 5 0 = 6 0 0”，每个数字单独成 token，说明代码模型的分词策略针对数字处理进行了专门设计。
2. Tokens and Embeddings.core: each digit is assigned its own token (so 600 becomes 6 0 0)

2. Tokens and Embeddings.point: 语言模型输出上下文相关的 token 向量
2. Tokens and Embeddings.explain: DeBERTa 模型对“Hello world”分词后输出每个 token 的上下文向量，演示了语言模型生成上下文嵌入的过程，证明其比静态词向量更具表达力。
2. Tokens and Embeddings.core: language models create contextualized word embeddings
2. Tokens and Embeddings.case:
tokens = tokenizer('Hello world', return_tensors='pt')
# Process the tokens
output = model(**tokens)[0]

2. Tokens and Embeddings.point: word2vec 对比训练思想可迁移到推荐系统
2. Tokens and Embeddings.explain: 将歌单视为句子、歌曲视为词，用 Word2Vec 训练歌曲向量，展示了 word2vec 思想在推荐系统中的迁移应用，证明其泛化能力。
2. Tokens and Embeddings.core: Imagine if we treated each song as we would a word or token, and we treated each playlist like a sentence.

2. Tokens and Embeddings.point: 模型输入是分词后的 token ID 而非原始文本
2. Tokens and Embeddings.explain: Phi-3 示例中，提示文本先被分词器转换为 input_ids 再输入模型生成，直观展示了模型实际接收的是 token ID 序列。
2. Tokens and Embeddings.core: A text prompt sent to the model is first broken down into tokens
2. Tokens and Embeddings.case:
prompt = "Write an email apologizing to Sarah for the tragic gardening mishap. Explain how it happened.<|assistant|>"
# Tokenize the input prompt
input_ids = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda")
# Generate the text
generation_output = model.generate(
input_ids=input_ids,
max_new_tokens=20
)

3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.core: If we give the model the ability to cache the results of the previous calculation (especially some of the specific vectors in the attention mechanism), we no longer need to repeat the calculations of the previous streams.
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.case: This comes out to 21.8 seconds. A dramatic difference. In fact, from a user experience standpoint, even the four-second generation time tends to be a long time to wait for a user that’s staring at a screen and waiting for an output from the model.
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.point: KV 缓存避免重复计算，是生成提速的关键
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.explain: 案例对比显示，启用 KV 缓存后生成时间从 21.8 秒降至约 4 秒，证明缓存能大幅减少重复计算，显著加速生成。

3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.point: Transformer LLM 一次只生成一个 token
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.explain: 用道歉邮件提示词演示模型逐 token 生成文本，直观体现自回归生成方式：每次前向计算只产出一个 token 并拼回输入。
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.core: A Transformer LLM generates one token at a time.
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.case:
prompt = "Write an email apologizing to Sarah for the tragic gardening mishap. Explain how it happened."
output = generator(prompt)
print(output[0]['generated_text'])

3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.point: KV 缓存显著加速生成过程
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.explain: 通过计时对比 use_cache=True 与关闭缓存的生成耗时（4.5 秒 vs 21.8 秒），量化证明 KV 缓存对生成速度的提升。
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.core: This is an optimization technique called the keys and values (kv) cache and it provides a significant speedup of the generation process.
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.case:
%%timeit -n 1
# Generate the text
generation_output = model.generate(
input_ids=input_ids,
max_new_tokens=100,
use_cache=True
)

3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.point: 注意力机制帮助模型引入上下文
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.explain: 在“狗追松鼠因为它”一句中，模型需借助注意力判断“它”指代谁，说明注意力机制能整合上下文信息来消解指代。
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.core: Attention is a mechanism that helps the model incorporate context as it’s processing a specific token.
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.case:
“The dog chased the squirrel because it”
For the model to predict what comes after “it,” it needs to know what “it” refers to. Does it refer to the dog or the squirrel?

3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.point: 语言建模头是一个简单的神经网络层
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.explain: 代码展示输入经模型主体和 LM head 得到下一个 token 的概率分布，具体说明 LM head 将隐藏状态映射为词表概率。
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.core: The LM head is a simple neural network layer itself.
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.case:
prompt = "The capital of France is"
# Tokenize the input prompt
input_ids = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").input_ids
# Tokenize the input prompt
input_ids = input_ids.to("cuda")
# Get the output of the model before the lm_head
model_output = model.model(input_ids)
# Get the output of the lm_head
lm_head_output = model.lm_head(model_output[0])

3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.point: 前馈神经网络是模型记忆与插值的来源
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.explain: 以“The Shawshank”预期生成“Redemption”为例，说明前馈网络存储并调用知识，是模型记忆信息的来源。
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.core: The feedforward neural network (collectively in all the model layers) is the source of this information
3. Looking Inside Large Language Models.case: A simple example giving the intuition of the feedforward neural network would be if we pass the simple input “The Shawshank” to a language model, with the expectation that it will generate “Redemption” as the most probable next word (in reference to the film from 1994).

4. Text Classification.core: We can describe our labels based on what they should represent. For example, a negative label for movie reviews can be described as “This is a negative movie review.”
4. Text Classification.case: An F1 score of 0.78 is quite impressive considering we did not use any labeled data at all! This just shows how versatile and useful embeddings are, especially if you are a bit creative with how they are used.
4. Text Classification.point: 把标签写成描述句再做向量，没有标注也能零样本分类
4. Text Classification.explain: 将标签描述为“This is a negative movie review.”等句子并编码为向量，与文本向量比较相似度，无需任何标注数据即达到F1 0.78，证明嵌入的零样本分类能力。

4. Text Classification.point: 用嵌入模型提取特征，再训练轻量分类器
4. Text Classification.explain: 冻结嵌入模型生成文本向量，仅用这些特征和标签训练逻辑回归分类器，形成两阶段方法，说明轻量分类器可高效利用嵌入特征。
4. Text Classification.core: Instead of directly using the representation model for classification, we will use an embedding model for generating features. Those features can then be fed into a classifier, thereby creating a two-step approach as shown in Figure 4-10.
4. Text Classification.case: We will keep this step straightforward and use a logistic regression as the classifier. To train it, we only need to use the generated embeddings together with our labels:

4. Text Classification.point: 任务专用表示模型可直接用于分类，并具跨域泛化能力
4. Text Classification.explain: 选用在推文上微调的Twitter-RoBERTa-base情感模型，虽未针对影评训练，仍可用于电影评论分类，展示任务专用模型的直接应用与泛化。
4. Text Classification.core: A task-specific model is a representation model, such as BERT, trained for a specific task, like sentiment analysis.
4. Text Classification.case: For the task-specific model, we are choosing the Twitter-RoBERTa-base for Sentiment Analysis model. This is a RoBERTa model fine-tuned on tweets for sentiment analysis. Although this was not trained specifically for movie reviews, it is interesting to explore how this model generalizes.

4. Text Classification.point: 生成式模型需通过提示指令完成分类
4. Text Classification.explain: 对Flan-T5每个文档前缀提示“Is the following sentence positive or negative?”，引导编码器-解码器模型输出情感标签，说明生成模型分类依赖指令。
4. Text Classification.core: Instead, we will have to instruct the model to do so.
4. Text Classification.case: Thus, we prefix each document with the prompt “Is the following sentence positive or negative?”:

4. Text Classification.point: 闭源生成模型可通过API与提示模板分类
4. Text Classification.explain: 通过OpenAI API调用ChatGPT，使用提示模板要求返回1或0，展示不加载本地模型即可用API完成文本分类。
4. Text Classification.core: Instead of loading the model, we can access the model through OpenAI’s API.
4. Text Classification.case:
prompt = """Predict whether the following document is a positive or negative movie review:
[DOCUMENT]
If it is positive return 1 and if it is negative return 0. Do not give any other answers.
"""

4. Text Classification.point: 本章以Rotten Tomatoes数据集进行二分类情感分析
4. Text Classification.explain: 使用包含5,331条正面和5,331条负面影评的rotten_tomatoes数据集，统一训练和评估各模型，为本章提供基准数据。
4. Text Classification.core: This means that we will focus on binary sentiment classification.
4. Text Classification.case: We will use the well-known “rotten_tomatoes” dataset to train and evaluate our models.1 It contains 5,331 positive and 5,331 negative movie reviews from Rotten Tomatoes.

5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.core: BERTopic is a topic modeling technique that leverages clusters of semantically similar texts to extract various types of topic representations.
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.case: For example, topic 0 contains the keywords “speech,” “asr,” and “recognition.” Based on these keywords, it seems that the topic is about automatic speech recognition (ASR).
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.point: BERTopic 先聚类再从簇中提取关键词，给每簇一个可读主题
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.explain: 案例展示主题0的关键词为 speech、asr、recognition，据此可判断该主题关于自动语音识别，证明从簇中提取关键词能生成可读主题。

5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.point: 密度聚类可自动发现大量语义簇
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.explain: HDBSCAN 在降维后的嵌入上运行，实际产出 156 个簇，说明聚类模型能自动将文档分组，无需预设类别数。
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.core: Find groups of semantically similar documents with a cluster model.
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.case:
hdbscan_model = HDBSCAN(
min_cluster_size=50, metric="euclidean", cluster_selection_method="eom"
).fit(reduced_embeddings)
clusters = hdbscan_model.labels_
# How many clusters did we generate?
len(set(clusters))
156

5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.point: 人工检查簇内容可理解聚类结果
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.explain: 检查簇0发现文档大多关于手语翻译，表明聚类结果具有可解释性，人工检查能确认簇的语义一致性。
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.caseTitle: 簇 0 的手语翻译论文
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.core: Text clustering is a powerful tool for finding structure among large collections of documents.
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.case: From these documents, it seems that this cluster contains documents mostly about translation from and to sign language, interesting!

5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.point: 聚类流水线第一步：用嵌入模型将文本转为向量
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.explain: 使用 gte-small 模型对摘要编码生成嵌入，展示文本转向量的具体实现，是后续降维和聚类的基础。
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.core: Convert the input documents to embeddings with an embedding model.

5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.point: 降维步骤用 UMAP 压缩嵌入维度
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.explain: UMAP 将嵌入降至 5 维并设置余弦距离等参数，说明降维是聚类前处理高维向量的关键步骤。
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.core: Reduce the dimensionality of embeddings with a dimensionality reduction model.
5. Text Clustering and Topic Modeling.case:
umap_model = UMAP(
n_components=5, min_dist=0.0, metric='cosine', random_state=42
)
reduced_embeddings = umap_model.fit_transform(embeddings)

6. Prompt Engineering.core: Chain-of-thought aims to have the generative model “think” first rather than answering the question directly without any reasoning.
6. Prompt Engineering.case: The cafeteria started with 23 apples. They used 20 apples, so they had 23 - 20 = 3 apples left. Then they bought 6 more apples, so they now have 3 + 6 = 9 apples. The answer is 9. Note how the model doesn’t generate only the answer but provides an explanation before doing so.
6. Prompt Engineering.point: 思维链让模型先推理再作答，提升复杂问题表现
6. Prompt Engineering.explain: 案例中模型先列出计算步骤（23-20=3，3+6=9）再给出答案，展示了思维链如何通过显式推理过程提升复杂问题的表现。

6. Prompt Engineering.point: 温度参数控制输出随机性
6. Prompt Engineering.explain: 设置temperature=1后每次运行输出不同，说明温度参数通过随机选择token引入随机性，影响生成文本的多样性。
6. Prompt Engineering.caseTitle: 温度参数控制输出随机性
6. Prompt Engineering.core: The temperature controls the randomness or creativity of the text generated.
6. Prompt Engineering.case:
# Using a high temperature
output = pipe(messages, do_sample=True, temperature=1)
print(output[0]["generated_text"])
Why don't chickens like to go on a rollercoaster? Because they're afraid they might suddenly become chicken-soup!
Note that every time you rerun this piece of code, the output will change! temperature introduces stochastic behavior since the model now randomly selects tokens.

7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.core: Although this method reduces the size of the chat history, it can only retain the last few conversations, which is not ideal for lengthy conversations.
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.case: Now that we have added another conversation we are up to three conversations. Considering the memory only retains the last two conversations, our very first question is not remembered. Since we provided an age in our first interaction, we check whether the LLM indeed does not know the age anymore:
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.point: 窗口记忆只保留最近几轮，控制了长度但会遗忘早期信息
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.explain: 案例中模型只保留最近两轮对话，因此第一轮提供的年龄信息被遗忘，无法再回答相关问题。
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.caseTitle: 忘掉年龄的聊天机器人

7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.point: 完整对话缓冲记忆让模型记住全部历史信息
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.explain: 通过追加完整对话历史，模型能根据之前提供的姓名正确回答“What is my name?”。
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.core: By extending the chain with memory, the LLM was able to use the chat history to find the name we gave it previously.
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.case:
llm_chain.invoke({"input_prompt": "What is my name?"})
{'input_prompt': 'What is my name?',
'chat_history': "Human: Hi! My name is Maarten. What is 1 + 1?\nAI: Hello Maarten! The answer to 1 + 1 is 2. Hope you're having a great day!",
'text': ' Your name is Maarten.'}

7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.point: ReAct代理交替推理与行动，调用工具完成多步任务
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.explain: 代理先搜索MacBook Pro价格，再用计算器按汇率换算成欧元，体现推理与行动相互影响。
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.core: ReAct merges these two concepts and allows reasoning to affect acting and actions to affect reasoning.

7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.point: 摘要记忆用LLM压缩历史，以摘要替代完整对话
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.explain: ConversationSummaryMemory 调用另一个 LLM 将整个对话历史提炼成要点，减少上下文长度。
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.core: As the name implies, this technique summarizes an entire conversation history to distill it into the main points.

7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.point: 顺序链将复杂任务拆成多个子任务依次生成
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.explain: 链只需用户输入一次，便依次生成标题、角色和故事三个组件，而非一次性生成全部内容。
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.core: Instead of generating everything in one go, we create a chain that only requires a single input by the user and then sequentially generates the three components.

7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.point: 用提示模板链避免重复复制提示模板
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.explain: 通过 PromptTemplate 定义一次模板，链即可复用，无需每次调用 LLM 时手动复制粘贴。
7. Advanced Text Generation Techniques a.core: Instead of having to copy-paste the prompt template each time we use the LLM, we would only need to define the user and system prompts.

8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.core: Notice that this wouldn’t have been possible if we were only doing keyword search because the top result did not include the same keywords in the query.
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.case: Note that the first result does not really answer the question despite it sharing the word “science” with the query.
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.point: 语义检索按含义匹配，能找到不含查询关键词的答案
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.explain: 稠密检索返回的星际穿越结果不含查询关键词，却因语义相近被召回，证明检索可超越关键词匹配。

8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.point: 纯关键词检索会因词语重合返回不相关结果
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.explain: BM25 检索将仅含“science”一词的影片简介排第一，未回答科学精确性问题，说明关键词匹配的局限。
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.core: Note that the first result does not really answer the question despite it sharing the word “science” with the query.

keyword_search(query = "how precise was the science")

8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.point: RAG 将检索结果作为上下文交给 LLM 生成有依据的答案
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.explain: Cohere 示例先检索相关文档，再让 LLM 基于文档回答收入问题，输出具体票房数字，体现接地生成。
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.core: We present the question and the top retrieved documents to the LLM, and ask it to answer the question given the context provided by the search results.
8. Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augment.case:
query = "income generated"
# 1- Retrieval
# We'll use embedding search. But ideally we'd do hybrid
results = search(query)

10. Creating Text Embedding Models.point: 硬负例是提升对比学习效果的关键
10. Creating Text Embedding Models.explain: 以阿姆斯特丹人口问题为例，构造相关但非答案的硬负例，说明如何让模型学会区分细微差别。

10. Creating Text Embedding Models.case: A good example of a hard negative is the following. Let’s assume we have the following question: “How many people live in Amsterdam?” A related answer to this question would be: “Almost a million people live in Amsterdam.” To generate a good hard negative, we ideally want the answer to contain something about Amsterdam and the number of people living in this city. For example: “More than a million people live in Utrecht, which is more than Amsterdam.” This answer relates to the question but is not the actual answer, so this would be a good hard negative.

10. Creating Text Embedding Models.case: The original cosine similarity loss example had a score of 0.72 with the full dataset. Using only 20% of that data, we managed to get a score of 0.71!

11. Fine-Tuning Representation Models fo.explain: Rotten Tomatoes 数据全量微调 BERT 得 F1 0.85，高于第4章任务专用模型的 0.80，且只需几分钟训练。

11. Fine-Tuning Representation Models fo.case: We get an F1 score of 0.85, which is quite a bit higher than the task-specific model we used in Chapter 4, which resulted in an F1 score of 0.80. It shows that fine-tuning a model yourself can be more advantageous than using a pretrained model. It only costs us a couple of minutes to train.

It demonstrates that although we generally want to train as many layers as possible, you can get away with training less if you do not have the necessary computing power.

11. Fine-Tuning Representation Models fo.core: Continuing pretraining on a pretrained BERT model has been shown to improve the performance of models in classification tasks and is a worthwhile addition to the fine-tuning pipeline.

12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.core: This means that we can find small ranks that approximate even the massive matrices of an LLM.
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.case: A 175B model like GPT-3, for example, would have a weight matrix of 12,288 × 12,288 inside each of its 96 Transformer blocks. That’s 150 million parameters. If we can successfully adapt that matrix into rank 8, that would only require two 12,288 × 2 matrices resulting in 197K parameters per block.
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.point: LLM 权重矩阵内在维度低，LoRA 用低秩矩阵即可大幅减少可训练参数
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.explain: GPT-3 每块权重矩阵 1.5 亿参数，用秩 8 分解后每块仅 19.7 万参数，直观展示低秩适配的压缩效果。

12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.point: QLoRA 通过量化大幅降低模型加载的显存需求
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.explain: 4 比特量化后加载模型仅需约 1 GB 显存，而未量化需约 4 GB，具体数字证明量化对显存的显著降低。
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.core: This is where we apply the Q in QLoRA, namely quantization.
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.case: This quantization procedure allows us to decrease the size of the original model while retaining most of the original weights’ precision. Loading the model now only uses ~1 GB VRAM compared to the ~4 GB of VRAM it would need without quantization.

12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.point: 人类评估是 LLM 评估的黄金标准
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.explain: Chatbot Arena 收集 80 多万人类投票计算胜率排名，体现人类评估在实际中作为黄金标准的应用规模。
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.core: Although benchmarks are important, the gold standard of evaluation is generally considered to be human evaluation.
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.case: At the time of writing, this method has generated over 800,000+ human votes that were used to compute a leaderboard. These votes are used to calculate the relative skill level of LLMs based on their win rates.

12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.point: 适配器微调只需极少参数即可接近全量微调效果
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.explain: BERT 仅微调 3.6% 参数，在 GLUE 上达到全量微调 0.4% 以内的性能，证明参数高效微调的有效性。
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.core: Adapters are a core component of many PEFT-based techniques.
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.case: Adapters are described in the paper “Parameter-efficient transfer learning for NLP”, which showed that fine-tuning 3.6% of the parameters of BERT for a task can yield comparable performance to fine-tuning all the model’s weights.1 On the GLUE benchmark, the authors show they reach within 0.4% of the performance of full fine-tuning.

12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.point: QLoRA 可实际用于指令微调开源小模型
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.explain: 用 QLoRA 对 TinyLlama 进行指令微调，展示本章方法在真实小模型上的完整实操流程。
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.core: Now that we have explored how QLoRA works, let us put that knowledge into practice!
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.case: In this section, we will fine-tune a completely open source and smaller version of Llama, TinyLlama, to follow instructions using the QLoRA procedure.

12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.point: 指令微调需按聊天模板准备指令数据
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.explain: 选取 3000 条文档按聊天模板格式化，说明指令数据准备的具体规模与模板化步骤。
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.core: To have the LLM follow instructions, we will need to prepare instruction data that follows a chat template.
12. Fine-Tuning Generation Models.case: We select a subset of 3,000 documents to reduce the training time, but you can increase this value to get more accurate results.
